quote.text: The wise use of leisure, it must be conceded, is a product of civilization and education.
quote.author: Bertrand Russell, “In Praise of Idleness”, Harper’s Magazine, October 1932

stories.kicker: The Good Life · Phillips Hong Kong Watch Auction
stories.headline: Patek 2499 makes HK$34.2 million at Phillips Hong Kong
stories.dek: Lot 958, the 1952 yellow-gold first series, sold on 21 November for HK$34,175,000 with premium, above its HK$12–24 million estimate and far past No. 169’s call.

stories.kicker: Screen & Sound · Sunrise on the Reaping
stories.headline: Sunrise on the Reaping takes $56 million on opening day
stories.dek: The Lionsgate prequel played 4,018 North American cinemas on Friday 20 November; trade projections put the weekend near US$120 million, clear of the $100 million mark.

stories.headline: Alexis Nikole Nelson puts TikTok foraging into a cookbook
stories.dek: Simon & Schuster published her Happy Snacking, Don’t Die! in September 2026; the Ohio forager has 4.9 million TikTok followers.

stories.headline: Araghchi says Iran is debating its no-bomb nuclear doctrine
stories.dek: In an interview published on 21 November, Iran’s foreign minister called the case for change “strong logic” while insisting policy stands. Nobody outside Iran knows where its 440.9kg of near-weapons-grade uranium is.

stories.headline: Singapore signs transport and green-industry pacts with China
stories.dek: Lawrence Wong met Premier Li Qiang in Beijing on 21 November. Li promised to “accelerate” the trade-pact upgrade, and more than 20 deliverables await the bilateral council later this month.

stories.kicker: The Atelier · Chopsticks In Lacquer And Wood
stories.headline: Chopstick maker Hyozaemon says most lacquer is plastic paint
stories.dek: Japan’s labelling code allows “lacquerware” only when every coat is urushi; Hyozaemon’s 100%-urushi kezuri pair costs ¥5,500 and is re-lacquered free.

stories.kicker: Technology · TSMC And China’s Chip Designers
stories.headline: TSMC halts advanced chip orders from Chinese designers
stories.dek: A US rule in force since 19 November pushes Chinese customers back to 28- and 40-nanometre lines; TSMC’s New York shares closed that day at 352.09 dollars, their lowest since April.

stories.headline: Grado cuts the cord on open-back headphones for US$329
stories.dek: The GW200, announced on 17 November and shipping in December, claims more than 60 hours a charge and plays through a wire when the battery is flat.

stories.kicker: Raising Them Well · Asking Children Directly
stories.headline: Teens and parents disagree on diagnoses, ABCD study finds
stories.dek: Among 11,868 American children followed from age 9 to 17, only one of the two reported a diagnosis in roughly 65 to 98 per cent of cases, JAMA Psychiatry published on 11 November.

stories.kicker: The Macro Desk · Where The Money Hid
stories.headline: Savers fled to US Treasuries, not gold or bitcoin
stories.dek: American bitcoin funds lost $1.25 billion in the five days to Friday 20 November while the ten-year Treasury yield slid from 5.15 to 4.92 per cent.

stories.kicker: Fitness · Light Band Training And Arteries
stories.headline: Light band training aids arteries, Ritsumeikan trial finds
stories.dek: Seventeen middle-aged and older Japanese adults did eight weeks of 45-minute elastic-band sessions; Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise published the results on 16 November.

stories.headline: Singapore Airlines opens its Western Sydney service on Monday
stories.dek: SQ261 leaves Changi at 11:30 on 23 November on a 303-seat A350; the 23:55 flight home works only because the new airport has no night curfew.

stories.kicker: The Diary · Stray Kids, Jump Festa And Tokyo
stories.headline: K-pop’s Stray Kids book two March nights at Kallang
stories.dek: Stray Kids lead as the biggest Singapore room here with every seat priced: S$168–378 for two nights, 6–7 March; Tokyo’s Friendship Run opens to overseas entrants on 1 December.

stories.kicker: The Undercurrent · China: The Fifteen-Hour School Day
stories.headline: Schools in Jiangsu push back gates after fifteen-hour days
stories.dek: Education chief Jiang Yong told a live phone-in on 27 October he felt “deeply guilty”; Chinese high schoolers average 68.6 hours of study a week — ten more than Britain let a teenage mill hand work from 1848.

stories.headline: Meridian held steady; headlines shortened, the cold-read score slipped
stories.dek: Headlines fell from 11.8 words to 9.0 across Nos. 163 to 169, and photographs rose from 10 to 18; the outside reader’s mean score fell from 4.09 to 3.73.
